For a `llms.txt` file, you want high-density technical information that highlights your systems engineering, optimization skills, and competitive wins.

### Top Projects
* **[VERITAS](https://github.com/eswar-7116/genai-media-verifier)** – Winner of CMR HackFest 3.0. A 4-engine GenAI forensics pipeline (Hugging Face, metadata, noise analysis) for deepfake detection. Optimized deployment via ML-dependency base-image extraction, reducing image size by 2.8 GB.
* **[Glambdar](https://github.com/eswar-7116/glambdar)** – High-performance serverless runtime in Go for Node.js functions. Implements adaptive EWMA for traffic prediction and proactive container pre-warming, achieving a 99.6% reduction in cold-start latency.
* **[Wiki Semantic Crawler](https://github.com/eswar-7116/wiki-semantic-crawler)** – Autonomous agent for the "Wiki Game" utilizing Weighted A* search. Uses `all-MiniLM-L6-v2` sentence transformer embeddings and cosine similarity as a heuristic for semantic pathfinding.
* **[Guntainer](https://github.com/eswar-7116/guntainer)** – Linux container runtime built from scratch in Go. Implements process isolation via namespaces, UID/GID remapping, and automated Alpine rootfs orchestration to demonstrate low-level OS mastery.
* **[Flux Interpreter](https://github.com/eswar-7116/flux-interpreter)** – Custom interpreted programming language engineered in Java. Features a hand-written lexer and recursive descent parser supporting variable environments, control flow, and arithmetic expressions.
